headline: Highest risk is medium: gpt-researcher can ingest files and browse, while PaddleOCR processes documents/images, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascade risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher reads files, runs browsers, and uses MCP; PaddleOCR processes documents/images. That creates a plausible default pathway where attacker-controlled document content or OCR output is fed into gpt-researcher as trusted text. No explicit provenance or isolation is shown for either agent, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is passed into gpt-researcher without provenance tagging
IF gpt-researcher ingests OCR text or documents as instructions
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and provenance label before passing OCR text
Disable automatic instruction-following on extracted document text
Review a sample OCR output before enabling the pipeline
Route untrusted documents through a human approval step
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher handles local documents and secrets and has broad network egress; PaddleOCR processes documents and images. If the same workspace or document set is shared, sensitive content can flow from A into B and then out through A's APIs or browser-based retrieval. The profiles do not show isolation, so the shared-data pathway is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same document workspace
IF sensitive documents are sent through PaddleOCR and then into gpt-researcher outputs
mitigations: Separate workspaces for OCR input and research output
Remove secrets from the shared document set
Turn off network egress for test runs
Inspect a single sample document end-to-end before scaling
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can run browsers, but only gpt-researcher is shown with filesystem read and subprocess spawning; PaddleOCR has allowlisted egress and no write capability is listed. The profiles do not show overlapping unrestricted writes or shared mutable resources, so direct capability conflict appears limited.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable browser session
mitigations: Keep one agent read-only
Use separate output directories
Avoid shared browser profiles
Run a quick lock test on the workspace
requires-engineering: add resource locking for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations, and PaddleOCR turns documents into extracted text. That makes a default cascade plausible where OCR output becomes authoritative input to research generation without verification. The profiles do not show a validation step between them, so the pair can amplify OCR mistakes into polished but wrong reports.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR text is fed directly into gpt-researcher as source material
IF no human or automated verification checks the extracted text before report generation
mitigations: Spot-check extracted text against the source PDF
Require citations back to page images
Reject low-confidence OCR segments
Compare one report against the original document manually
requires-engineering: add verification gates between extraction and writing

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, and both are open-source. However, gpt-researcher handles secrets and local documents while PaddleOCR handles documents/images, so compliance risk exists if regulated content is routed through both without policy controls. The evidence is insufficient for medium, so this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed by both agents under different retention policies
IF EU or PHI data is routed through the pair without a documented DPA or residency control
mitigations: Classify documents before processing
Block regulated data in a test run
Document retention settings for both tools
Keep audit logs of document movement
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
